DIAGNOSIS READY: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features.

The patient is a 23-year-old female presenting with a 4-month history of persistent sadness, significant weight loss, insomnia, and impaired concentration, accompanied by auditory hallucinations of a persecutory and nihilistic nature. Given the severity of the depressive symptoms and the presence of psychotic features, this presentation meets the criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features rather than Schizophrenia, as the mood symptoms are prominent and the psychosis appears mood-congruent. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the clear clinical picture of major depression with psychotic features.
